expectations.text: The response rejects not replying; every request gets an answer, including declines.
expectations.evidence: 'Do not stay silent.' 'Silence is the one option the skill names as an exposure.' A decline email template is provided.

expectations.text: It requires the reply sent immediately rather than sat on, because a late decline consumes the attendee's remaining planning window.
expectations.evidence: 'sends the email in Part 1 within the hour'; 'A late decline is worse than an early one because it has already used up the attendee's planning window.'

expectations.text: The reply offers what does exist instead (for example reserved front seating, any live transcript option, advance materials) rather than nothing.
expectations.evidence: 'Here is what we can do: <live captioning, a reserved seat near the front, session notes in advance...>'

expectations.text: It refuses to present stream auto-captions as an equivalent substitute for requested interpretation, while still checking real near-term options such as remote interpretation or a live captioner before declining.
expectations.evidence: 'Auto-captions are not an interpretation substitute'; Part 2 steps on remote interpreting and live human captioning.

expectations.text: A named person decides the decline and the reason is written down, so the decline is a decision rather than a silence.
expectations.evidence: 'One named person decides a decline, and writes the reason down.'

expectations.text: The reply states whether the answer changes for the next edition, and the case is committed to the debrief record.
expectations.evidence: 'We will publish interpretation as a bookable option with a stated lead time next year'; 'Keep a log: requested, delivered, declined and why.'

expectations.text: It identifies 'accommodations available upon request' as the root failure: no stated lead time, no named owner, and the whole burden of imagination placed on the person who has to ask.
expectations.evidence: 'It gave you no lead time and no idea what we offer'; 'Replace "accommodations available upon request" with specific scope and a lead time'.

expectations.text: The rewritten published wording includes a booking lead time in weeks, a request-by date, a named owner to write to, and a commitment to confirm within a stated number of days either way.
expectations.evidence: 'tell us by <date> and write to <named owner>. We need <N> weeks to book and will confirm within <M> days either way.'

expectations.text: It applies data handling to Tomas's disclosure: shared only with the organizers arranging the request, kept until a stated date, then deleted.
expectations.evidence: 'We use what you tell us only to arrange your accommodation. Only the organizers who need it... We will delete it <two weeks after the event>.'

expectations.text: It carries the request forward: a need that recurs edition to edition becomes a planned provision next time rather than a repeat request.
expectations.evidence: 'requests carried forward'; Part 5 'Offer interpretation on request... Pre-book a relationship... Hold a contingency budget line'.

expectations.text: The next-edition plan publishes the provision page before the travel-booking window, since a page published after attendees book reaches nobody it was for.
expectations.evidence: 'Publish one accessibility page before attendees book travel... A page published after people booked reached nobody it was for.'
